newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps drift, market ponders OPEC quota talk.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps drift, market ponders OPEC quota talk.

text.p: European oil swaps were broadly steady on Wednesday bar Brent CFDs which showed a slight softness as the market pondered OPEC quota talk.
News from Vienna was of OPEC heavyweights Saudi Arabia and Iran turning up the heat on the cartel's quota violators in a move to curb overproduction and support oil prices.

Brent CFDs eased back a touch with June 30-July 4 and July 7-14 both hovering around -40 cents against August from -35 cents on Tuesday. Further out July 14-18 was very narrowly weaker at -36 cents from -35 cents and July 21-25 eased to -32 cents from -30 cents.
Gas oil crack spreads held steady on 4Q97 at $4.45, a touch firmer on 1Q98 at $4.65 and unchanged on 2Q98 at $4.10.
Heavy fuel swaps saw bids and offers widen. Dealers said July was bid at $81.50 and offered at $83.50.
"I don't think we have any 50 cent spreads," said one.
August was about $1 apart with offers at $84.50. No paper was thought traded, but physical barges went at $82.50, $83.00 and $84.00.

Gasoline held steady with July, August and September all flat at $178.50 value. A prompt Antwerp barge sold at $181 fob. Naphtha was also unchanged with July at $173 and August and September showing contangoes of $1 and $2 respectively.
